name: Northern Luri
notes: Northern Luri (لۊری شومالی) — Southwestern Iranian language of Iran (Lorestan and neighbouring provinces), written in a Perso-Arabic (Arabic-script) alphabet with additional letters for Luri consonants and vowels. SKELETON: consonant/vowel-letter table now specified, based on the shared Persian-alphabet consonant inventory (as `fa` already documents) plus the two extra letters attested in Luri and Kurdish Perso-Arabic orthographic practice for the rhotic and lateral contrasts also found in neighbouring Kurdish varieties: ⟨ڕ⟩ for the strong/trilled rhotic /r/ (vs. the plain tap ⟨ر⟩ /ɾ/) and ⟨ڵ⟩ for the velarised/dark lateral /ɫ/ (vs. plain ⟨ل⟩ /l/), matching the same rhotic and lateral contrast the `ku` (Kurmanji) spec documents for a closely related Iranian variety of the same dialect-contact area (Anonby 2003, 'Update on Luri: How Many Languages?'). As an ABJAD, short vowels are normally unwritten, so this table cannot by itself vocalise unvowelled text — the same INPUT CONTRACT limitation documented for `fa`/`ar`. STRESS EXEMPTION: no `stress` block is declared; Northern Luri word-stress is not reconstructible from unvocalised Perso-Arabic spelling.
